Reference material is **information-oriented**: descriptions of the
machinery and facts you consult while working — organised for lookup,
not reading order.

## Available reference

### [Glossary](glossary.qmd)

Definitions of the terms this project uses consistently.

### [Measurement framework](measurement-framework.qmd)

Domains mapped to candidate indicator families and likely sources
(provisional, milestone M1).

### [Data sources](data-sources.qmd)

The catalogue of catalogued data sources: form, coverage, licence,
access, resolution, and quality notes (milestone M2, in progress).

### [Data quality](data-quality.qmd)

Known gaps, revisions, suppressions, and definitional breaks in the
catalogued sources.

### [Indicator: Mortality rates, British Columbia](indicator-mortality-rates-bc.qmd)

The project's first published indicator, with provenance, caveats, and a
regenerable chart.

### [Indicator: Life expectancy at birth, British Columbia](indicator-life-expectancy-bc.qmd)

Life expectancy at birth by sex (1980–2024), the project's second
published indicator, from Statistics Canada's complete life table.

### [Project structure](project-structure.qmd)

What lives where in the repository and how the documentation site is
organised.

### Planned

- **Data source catalogue** — every data source: coverage, licence,
  access route, refresh cadence, and source form (microdata, summary
  statistics, dashboard, or report). "Data" is construed broadly: the
  aim is the best use of all publicly available information that can be
  appropriately used (milestone M2).
- **Indicator reference pages** — one page per indicator: definition,
  unit, population, provenance, caveats (milestones M1–M3).
- **Methods reference** — statistical and causal methods used, with
  parameters (milestones M4–M5).
